headline: Spatial and genetic dependence now inform pathogen transmission inference
label: Spatial Dependence In Transmission Inference
summary: February 2026 preprints encode host mobility, spatio-temporal priors, and viral haplotype similarity into transmission inference models.
synthesis: The shared thread is explicit representation of spatial or relational dependence when inferring transmission from epidemiological and genetic data. A metapopulation model on a high-resolution human mobility network reproduces the 2010 New Zealand kiwifruit Psa-V outbreak and tests surveillance and importation timing, placing spread on the mobility graph. DENcode estimates pairwise dengue transmission probabilities by combining viral haplotype genetic similarity with temperature-modulated epidemiological inputs. STOEP fuses learned and expert spatio-temporal priors for COVID-19 and influenza forecasting and beats the best baseline by 11.1% RMSE. What is new is treating host arrangement, location, and genetic relatedness as informative rather than assuming independence among observations. The systems differ in host, pathogen, and scale, so the common element is methodological rather than a single biological question.
